# requireValidVersion

<link-summary>Returns the value as a version string, or throws.</link-summary>

<web-summary>requireValidVersion() — Returns the value as a version string, or throws. apps-script-utils, English.</web-summary>

<tldr>
<p>Module: <code>lang/string</code> · Since: 1.11.0</p>
</tldr>

```typescript
function requireValidVersion(
  value: string | null | undefined,
  message: string = "Expected a valid version."
): string;
```

Dot-separated groups of digits, any number of them. A pre-release suffix, a leading `v` and an empty group are all rejected, so `"1.2.3-beta"` does not pass even though SemVer allows it.

`isX` and `nonX` answer a question and never interrupt control flow; `requireX` and `requireNonX` hand the value back or throw. The scheme is explained in [](validation-conventions.md).

## Parameters

| Parameter                                              | Type                          | Description                                                   |
| :----------------------------------------------------- | :---------------------------- | :------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `value`                                                | `string \| null \| undefined` | The value to validate.                                        |
| `message` _(optional)_ `= "Expected a valid version."` | `string`                      | The message of the exception. A default is used when omitted. |

## Returns

`string` — the same value, typed as a version string.

## Throws

| Exception                  | Condition                          |
| :------------------------- | :--------------------------------- |
| `IllegalArgumentException` | the value is not a version string. |

## Examples

### What passes and what does not

```javascript
requireValidVersion("1"); // => "1"
requireValidVersion("1.2.3"); // => "1.2.3"
requireValidVersion("1.2.3-beta"); // throws IllegalArgumentException
requireValidVersion("v1.2"); // throws IllegalArgumentException
```
